title: Task-completion-rate suite (Pass1/Pass5, STATE-Bench-shaped)
summary: benchmarks/agent_quality/tasks.py: a small multi-turn task suite run 5x each, with-SDK vs. flat-context vs. no-memory, reporting Pass1 (best-of-5) and Pass5 (all-5-succeed) task-success rates — the end-task metric this repo has never measured.
description:
Every existing suite measures Q&A retrieval correctness (does `search()` return the right fact / does the judge mark the answer CORRECT), never whether a *multi-step task* that depends on recalling stored memory actually completes end-to-end. Build `benchmarks/agent_quality/tasks.py`: a small set (start with 10-15, matching the existing per-category density in `benchmarks/retrieval_quality/dataset.py`) of multi-turn agentic tasks that require correctly recalling and *acting on* stored memory across turns — e.g. 'the user told you their deployment env in session 1 and asked you to change a config value in session 2; do it without asking again' — extending, not duplicating, the LongMemEval-shaped scenarios EPIC-16 already builds against the real dataset.

Each task is attempted 5 times per condition (reuse the existing judge's temperature/sampling settings; BENCH-1 already confirmed local-Ollama judge non-determinism across repeated runs, which is exactly the noise Pass¹/Pass⁵ is designed to characterize rather than hide). Report, per Microsoft's STATE-Bench terminology: **Pass¹** — average success rate across the 5 attempts (best-effort capability), **Pass⁵** — percentage of tasks succeeding on all 5 attempts (stability/reliability). Run three conditions to isolate memory's actual contribution: with-SDK (`store.remember()`/`search()`), flat-context baseline (matches `run_baseline()`'s existing pattern in `benchmarks/retrieval_quality/run.py`), and no-memory-at-all (the agent gets no cross-session information whatsoever — a new third condition this repo has never run, needed because flat-context is not the same as 'no memory system helped').

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Suite runs headlessly via the existing benchmark CLI pattern (`--suite agent_quality` or similar, matching `scripts/run_benchmarks.py`'s existing `--suite` flag shape).
- Pass¹ and Pass⁵ reported per task and aggregated, for all three conditions.
- Task definitions are deterministic/reproducible under a fixed seed, matching the existing `--seed 42` convention.

**Definition of Done:**
- Results appended to BENCHMARKS.md as part of the new Suite 4 (AGQ-5 owns the final wiring; this story can land its own results section first if AGQ-5 isn't ready).
- Depends on AGQ-1 (metric definitions) and EPIC-16's BM-16 (real dataset infra this suite's scenarios extend). Independent of AGQ-3/AGQ-4.
